description.en: Build dynamic web pages with Django views, URL routing, template inheritance, and the Jinja2-like template language.
description.ta: Django பார்வைகள், URL ரூட்டிங், வார்ப்புரு மரபுரிமை மற்றும் Jinja2 போன்ற வார்ப்புரு மொழியுடன் மாறும் வலை பக்கங்களை உருவாக்குங்கள்.

story_variants.en:
## The Printing Press

Vaathiyaar holds up two pages. "A **view** decides WHAT data to show. A **template** decides HOW to show it. The view is the brain, the template is the face."

### Function-Based Views (FBV)
```python
def post_list(request):
    posts = Post.objects.all()
    return render(request, 'blog/post_list.html', {'posts': posts})
```

### Class-Based Views (CBV)
```python
class PostListView(ListView):
    model = Post
    template_name = 'blog/post_list.html'
    context_object_name = 'posts'
```

### Template Language

| Syntax | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|----------|
| `{{ var }}` | Output a variable | `{{ post.title }}` |
| `{% tag %}` | Logic tags | `{% for post in posts %}` |
| `{% if %}` | Conditionals | `{% if user.is_authenticated %}` |
| `{{ var\|filter }}` | Transform output | `{{ text\|truncatewords:30 }}` |
| `{% extends %}` | Inheritance | `{% extends 'base.html' %}` |
| `{% block %}` | Overridable sections | `{% block content %}` |

### Template Inheritance
```
base.html          ← Master layout (nav, footer)
  └── post_list.html  ← Extends base, fills {% block content %}
      └── post_detail.html ← Also extends base
```

> **Key Concept:** Template inheritance eliminates code duplication. Define the layout once in base.html, then override only the parts that change in child templates.

steps.line:
# blog/urls.py
from django.urls import path
from . import views

urlpatterns = [
    path('', views.PostListView.as_view(), name='post-list'),
    path('post/<int:pk>/', views.post_detail, name='post-detail'),
]

explanation.en: URL captures the post ID as an integer parameter 'pk'
The base template defines the overall page structure

under_the_hood.summary: A view gathers data and calls render(), which finds the template file, compiles it into a tree of nodes, and renders that tree with a context dict, escaping every variable for HTML along the way.

steps.title: render() is three steps in one
steps.body: render(request, 'blog/post_list.html', {'posts': posts}) asks the template loaders for the file (with APP_DIRS on, it searches each app's templates/ folder), renders it with the context, and wraps the resulting string in an HttpResponse with status 200.

steps.title: Templates compile into nodes
steps.body: The template engine splits the text into tokens: plain text, {{ variables }} and {% tags %}. It builds a node list where a {% for post in posts %} tag becomes a ForNode holding its inner nodes. Rendering walks that tree; production setups cache compiled templates so this parsing happens once.

steps.title: Dot lookups try several things
steps.body: {{ post.title }} resolves by trying, in order, a dictionary lookup post['title'], then an attribute post.title, then a list index if the part is a number. If the attribute is a method with no arguments, Django calls it. A missing value renders as an empty string instead of raising an error.

steps.title: Autoescaping protects the page
steps.body: Every variable is HTML-escaped on output: a title of <script>alert(1)</script> is written as <script>alert(1)</script>, so the browser shows it as text instead of running it. The |safe filter switches this off and should only be used on HTML you generated yourself.

steps.title: Class-based views dispatch on the method
steps.body: PostListView.as_view() returns an ordinary function for urls.py. On each request it creates a view instance and calls dispatch(), which picks get() or post() from request.method. ListView's get() calls get_queryset(), then get_context_data() (adding object_list and post_list), then renders the template, so you only override the step you need.

under_the_hood.takeaway: Views decide what data to show; templates are compiled node trees that turn that data into escaped HTML. render() is the glue, and class-based views are the same steps split into overridable methods.
